questions.question: What happens if you downcast to an incorrect type without checking with instanceof?
options: The object is converted to the correct type
explanations: Correct. Without instanceof, the cast fails at runtime with ClassCastException.
It does not fail at compile time.

questions.question: If Animal a = new Dog(), which methods can 'a' call WITHOUT a downcast?
options: All methods of Animal and Dog
explanations: It cannot call Dog-exclusive methods without a cast.
Correct. It can only access methods defined in Animal (the reference type).

questions.question: Can an abstract class have constructors?
options: Yes, so subclasses can call super()
Only if it has concrete methods
explanations: Correct. Although it is not instantiated directly, its constructors are used via super() in subclasses.
It can have constructors regardless of whether it has concrete methods.
